newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks correct in volatile trade, volume up.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks correct in volatile trade, volume up.

text.p: Greek stocks ended 0.44 percent lower on Tuesday on heavy volume with market watchers saying it was a normal correction with the heavy 21.1 billion drachma turnover an indication of active interest in the stock market.

"We saw a correction taking place twice on Tuesday, with the index ending down. Volume was heavy and showed the market was very active. Resistance at 1,120 was overcome but the market dipped. I see support at the 1,080 level," said broker Iakovos Diamandopoulos at Hermes Brokerage.
The correction could probably have more to go in the next few sessions, but the market will keep its momentum as it has already attracted funds, Diamandopoulos added.

"Tuesday's correction was a healthy reaction to the bourse's 2.78 percent rise on Monday. Market sentiment is good but the rise was a bit too fast," said Yianna Tziovara, an assistant portfolio manager at Allianz Mutual Funds.
She added that blue chips, such as bank shares and Titan TTNr.AT continued to perform well.
The Athens general share index closed 0.44 percent or 4.90 points down at 1109.01 from Monday's 1113.91, after opening at 1116.94.
Banks gained 0.39 percent, construction lost 0.96 percent and investment shares ended flat. Small caps ended 3.14 percent down with industrials slipping 0.30 percent.
Tuesday's turnover was high at 21.1 billion drachmas on volume of 5.9 million shares. Losers led gainers 146 to 71 with 29 issues unchanged on 246 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 899.00-917.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, lost 140 drachmas to close at 5,250.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $18.33-$19.33. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 7,232-7,695 drachmas. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
